question: Will any presidential candidate win outright in the first round of the Brazil election?
resolution_criteria:
Presidential elections are scheduled to be held in Brazil on October 4, 2026. A second round will be held if no candidate secures more than 50% of the valid votes in the first round.

This market will resolve to "Yes" if any candidate wins this election in the first round. Otherwise, this market will resolve to "No".

If the result of the first round of this election isn't known by June 30, 2027, 11:59 PM ET, the market will resolve to "No".

This market will resolve based on the result of the election as indicated by a consensus of credible reporting. If there is ambiguity, this market will resolve based solely on the official results as reported by the Brazilian government, specifically the Superior Electoral Court (Tribunal Superior Eleitoral, TSE) (e.g., https://dadosabertos.tse.jus.br/).
research:
I couldn't confirm any September 2026 poll. The latest poll data I could verify is from May 2026, and it shows Lula leading the first round well short of the 50% of valid votes needed to win outright. Many search results were dated after 2026-09-26, so I left them out as you asked.

## 1. Resolution source
- The question is decided by the TSE's official results (dadosabertos.tse.jus.br) or by a consensus of credible reporting. A candidate needs more than 50% of valid votes, which excludes blank and spoiled ballots. As of 2026-09-26 the vote (October 4) has not happened, so there are no results. I did not fetch the TSE site because the first round is still ahead.

## 2. Current status
- Nothing has settled the question yet. The main candidates are Lula (PT) and Flávio Bolsonaro (PL). Others in the race include Ronaldo Caiado, Romeu Zema, Renan Santos and Augusto Cury, and at different points pollsters also tested Ciro Gomes and Ratinho Júnior. With that many candidates, every poll I found leaves the leader below 50% of valid votes.

## 3. Recent news (newest first)
- I could not find any first-round poll from September 2026 published before 2026-09-26. Searches kept returning later material, which I excluded. The forecaster should check Datafolha, Quaest and AtlasIntel for releases from 1 to 25 September.
- 2026-07/08: Wikipedia's polling table lists a Quaest poll from late July to early August with the top two at 39 and 30, probably Lula 39%, Flávio 30%. The column labels were unclear, so this needs checking. [Wikipedia polling](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Opinion_polling_for_the_2026_Brazilian_presidential_election)
- 2026-05-05: Real Big Data, scenario without Ciro: Lula 48%, Flávio 34%, Caiado 5%, Zema 4%, measured as total votes. [Bem Paraná](https://www.bemparana.com.br/noticias/politica/lula-e-flavio-bolsonaro-empatam-em-1o-e-2o-turnos-aponta/), [Jovem Pan](https://jovempan.com.br/noticias/politica/realtime-bigdata-lula-empata-com-flavio-caiado-e-ciro-em-eventual-2o-turno.html)
- 2026-05: Futura/Apex: Lula 42.7%, Flávio 35.6% in the first round. [CNN Brasil](https://www.cnnbrasil.com.br/eleicoes/futura-apex-lula-tem-427-e-flavio-356-no-1o-turno/)
- 2026-04: AtlasIntel/Bloomberg: Lula 46.6%, Flávio 39.7%, Caiado 3.3%. [Portal de Prefeitura](https://portaldeprefeitura.com.br/eleicoes/lula-lidera-primeiro-turno-empata-flavio-zema-atlas/620180/)
- 2026-03: Datafolha: Lula led every first-round scenario, and in a runoff Lula had 46% to Flávio's 43%. [Yahoo/Reuters](https://www.yahoo.com/news/articles/flavio-bolsonaro-draws-even-lula-161733328.html)
- 2026-01: Genial/Quaest: Lula 35%, Flávio 26%, Ratinho Jr. 9%. [Quaest via tagteam](https://tagteam.harvard.edu/hub_feeds/3884/feed_items/17183858/content)
- Across these polls, Lula leads the first round by about 7 to 14 points but stays in the 35-48% range of total votes. Runoff simulations are mostly technical ties, which suggests a closely split electorate.

## 4. Base rates
- Since 1989, Brazil has held 9 direct presidential elections. Two were won in the first round: Fernando Henrique Cardoso in 1994 and 1998. The other seven went to a runoff: 1989, 2002, 2006, 2010, 2014, 2018 and 2022. The last first-round win was 28 years ago.
- 2022: Lula took 48.4% of valid votes to Bolsonaro's 43.2%, and the race went to a runoff even though Lula slightly beat his poll numbers. The polls underestimated Bolsonaro. [Inquirer/AFP](https://newsinfo.inquirer.net/1674150/brazil-election-goes-to-runoff-as-bolsonaro-beats-polls/amp)
- 2006: Lula got 48.6% and was forced into a runoff, even though some final polls showed him close to an outright win.

## 5. Other forecasts
- Polymarket has this exact market ("Will any presidential candidate win outright in the first round of the Brazil election?"). An aggregator snapshot showed "Yes" at about 13¢. I could not confirm the date of that snapshot, so it may not reflect the price on 2026-09-26. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/0x087469b4129c64c688397028059dfd366796adbd426e0079ee4cfdd2e4a07b61)
- Kalshi has a matching market, KXBRAZILPRES1R-26OCT04. I could not get its current price. [SimpleFunctions](https://simplefunctions.dev/markets/KXBRAZILPRES1R-26OCT04)
- There is also a related Polymarket market on the first-round margin of victory. [Lines.com](https://www.lines.com/prediction-markets/elections/brazil-presidential-election-first-round-margin-of-victory)
- I found no expert or model forecast.

## 6. Upcoming events before resolution
- The final polls from Datafolha, Quaest, AtlasIntel and MDA are expected in the last week before October 4. Brazilian pollsters keep publishing until election eve.
- The final TV debates take place in the last week of the campaign.
- Late tactical voting ("voto útil") could squeeze the smaller candidates, which would make an outright win more likely. An outright win would need the leader at roughly 50%+ of valid votes, about 3-5 points above the best recent poll numbers I could verify.
- The first round is on 2026-10-04, and the TSE count usually finishes the same night.

forecasts.reasoning:
- Late tactical voting ("voto útil") could squeeze Caiado, Zema and Renan Santos.
- For No:
  - Quaest (late July to early August 2026) had Lula at about 39% to Flávio's 30%, with a sizeable share for other candidates.
  - Datafolha (2026-03) and others show runoff technical ties, such as 46-43. A candidate who only ties in a two-way race almost never clears 50% of valid votes when the field is fragmented.
  - The polls underestimated the Bolsonaro camp in 2022.
  - Polymarket's Yes price was about 13% on an undated snapshot.

(e) **Scenarios**
- No: Lula finishes around 45-48% of valid votes, Flávio around 38-42%, and minor candidates take 10-15%. The race goes to a runoff on October 25. This mirrors 2006 and 2022.
- Yes: The minor candidates collapse in the final week, anti-Bolsonaro voters consolidate early, and abstention among Flávio-leaning voters is high. Lula reaches 50.3% of valid votes.

(f) **From base rate to final probability**
- I start at about 12%, the polarized-era base rate, which roughly matches the market at about 13%.
- I adjust down slightly for three reasons:
  - The runoff ties put Lula's first-round ceiling near 50%.
  - The latest verified poll (Quaest, around August) had him well below that.
  - There is a recent pattern of underestimating the right.
- I keep a meaningful tail because some polls (Real Big Data, AtlasIntel) imply a valid-vote share close to 50%, and I could not verify any September polls.
- The result is about 9%.

Probability: 9%
